strategyPosture: Selective and patient into the Oct 27-28 FOMC: the index is calm (SPY 1.4% off its high, VIX 15.91) but rates are restrictive (10-year 5.11%) and leadership is rotating, so no chasing. The only offensive work is research on the quality AI-infra dislocation — AVGO, NVDA, VRT — where fundamentals are ahead of price; the speculative nuclear unwind is a watch, not a catch.

themes.counterRead: The concentration engine's read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: leadership is rotating away from the mega-caps without the credit deterioration that historically confirms a broad rollover. The divergence itself is the risk to track — credit conditions can flip, and if they do, this same gap becomes the rollover signature.
themes.dataAnchor: Underneath, the Mag7 averages 10.93% below its 52-week highs against SPY's 1.4%, a 9.53-point divergence gap; TSLA is the weakest at 26.5% below its high while AAPL sits just 1% below. But bank lending standards are LOOSE — SLOOS at 0%, far below the ~40% stress zone — and high-yield spreads are a calm 3.25%.
themes.label: Leadership rotation, not rollover — Mag7 lag is real, credit says no break
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY at $771.44, only 1.4% below its 52-week high — so the market story is that nothing is wrong and the bull market is intact.
themes.watchFor: The Mag7–SPY divergence gap widening beyond 12 points from today's 9.53, or SLOOS tightening off 0% — either flips this from rotation to rollover risk.

themes.counterRead: Credit and volatility refuse to confirm stress: HY OAS is 3.25% and the VIX fell 3.34% today to 15.91. The market is repricing the policy path, not pricing a credit accident — so the CPI shock is a duration problem concentrated in long-multiple names, not a systemic one, unless spreads start moving.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve is genuinely restrictive: 10-year at 5.11%, 30-year at 5.45%, real 10-year at 2.79%, 2s10s only +0.29. QQQ is down 0.96% today against SPY's 0.05% dip — duration is taking the hit, exactly as a rates shock should distribute it.
themes.label: Hot September CPI meets a restrictive curve — rates are the binding constraint into the Oct 27-28 FOMC
themes.narrative: September CPI ran above forecasts, and the tape narrative is rate-hike fear: Nasdaq down on the print, chipmakers sinking on inflation data, and the Oct 27-28 FOMC now priced as a live risk event.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS widening past 3.75% from 3.25%, or the 10-year pushing above 5.25% into the Oct 27-28 FOMC — either converts a duration repricing into a broad risk event.

themes.counterRead: This is the DATA_AHEAD pattern: price is discounting a thesis break that the revenue and cash-flow data do not show. The honest caveat is timing — these names are falling into a hot-CPI, pre-FOMC window, and a dislocation is not an entry signal by itself; the standing posture is research-screened, verify the thesis before any sizing.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals point the other way. AVGO is 31.7% below its high while revenue grows 55% YoY with a 67.8% gross margin and $26.9B of free cash flow — the engine's top conviction score at 81. NVDA carries a conviction promotion at 82 with revenue growing 61.4% YoY and sits only 11.1% off its peak. VRT is 44.6% below its high on revenue growth of 27.7%, with RSI washed out at 28.6.
themes.label: AI-infrastructure quality is being sold like the thesis broke — revenue says it didn't
themes.narrative: The AI buildout trade is being unwound: the chip and infra complex sank on the CPI print, and the prevailing story is that AI capex names were a rates bubble now deflating.
themes.watchFor: VRT and AVGO stabilizing with RSI recovering through 35 while revenue signals hold — versus a fresh leg down through today's levels, which would say the selling is information, not dislocation.

themes.counterRead: The complex is separating into story stocks and cash stocks, and only the story leg is collapsing. The caution runs both ways: VST's own revenue inflection is flagged DETERIORATING in the screen, so its relative strength is not a clean bill of health — it is the least-bad leg of a theme whose narrative ran ahead of its fundamentals.
themes.dataAnchor: The speculative leg is in a real unwind: SMR is down 32.5% in a month, OKLO down 25.2%, URA down 15.0%. But VST — the name with actual cash flows — is a 1-month leader at +7.2%, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, and it trades at 2.9x sales with $1.3B of free cash flow, 26.8% below its high.
themes.label: Pre-revenue nuclear is unwinding hard — cash-generative power is not following it down
themes.narrative: The nuclear/AI-power story was priced as a straight line up: SMR, OKLO and the uranium complex carried the theme, and VST was swept along as the listed proxy.
themes.watchFor: SMR/OKLO month trends flattening off −25% to −32% (unwind exhausting) versus VST breaking below its 1-month trend — the latter would say the unwind is spreading from story to cash names.

themes.counterRead: Capital is not leaving equities; it is rotating into cash-generative quality — payment rails, specialty insurance, grid services — while it waits out the rates question. That is consistent with the ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER read and argues the index calm is earned, not complacent — but it also means leadership is narrow in a different place than the index weights assume.
themes.dataAnchor: Something does lead: Mastercard is the #1 one-month performer in the tracked universe at +9.85%, up 0.83% today while QQQ falls. The same pattern shows in the conviction screen — KNSL scores 77 on 18% revenue growth and a 26.9% FCF margin, PWR screens as a multiple-compression dislocation at 19.6% below its high with a constructive 1-month trend.
themes.label: Cash-generative quality is quietly leading the tape — MA at the top of the leader board
themes.narrative: With mega-cap tech lagging and speculative themes unwinding, the market story is defensive drift — nothing leads, everything waits for the FOMC.
themes.watchFor: MA holding its 1-month leadership (+9.85%) through the FOMC; if even the quality rails roll over while Mag7 lags, the rotation read fails and breadth is genuinely breaking.

watchFor: HY OAS widening past 3.75% from today's 3.25% — the signal that rotation is becoming rollover.
10-year Treasury above 5.25% (from 5.11%) or a hawkish hike-risk signal at the Oct 27-28 FOMC.
Mag7–SPY 52-week-high divergence gap widening beyond 12 points from 9.53.
VRT/AVGO RSI recovering through 35 with revenue signals intact — dislocation stabilizing; a fresh leg down says the selling is information.
IWM arresting its slide (−3.59% 1m, −6.9% 3m vs SPY +1.16% 1m) — small-cap stabilization would confirm breadth repair under the rotation.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds around the FOMC: with a real 10-year at 2.79% and a hot CPI behind it, a hawkish surprise lands first on the already-unwinding speculative complex, while any dovish relief squeezes the most oversold quality names — VRT at RSI 28.6 — the hardest.
